title: First-component extraction with linear space
statement: There are a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the first component parsed from $x$ by the aligned pair parser, or the empty word if parsing fails. At every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, its computation on $x$ uses at most $c(|x|+1)$ work-tape cells.
